newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Concert scores over rival Global One.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Concert scores over rival Global One.

text.p: The Concert telecoms alliance scored a point over rival Global One by signing up Telefonica of Spain and may now be better placed to line up an Asian partner, analysts said on Friday.
But the contest is not yet over and Global One, an alliance of France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint, could soon make announcements of its own, they added.
"We do not comment on other operators' activities," said a France Telecom spokeswoman in Paris and a spokeswoman for Global One in Brussels also had "no comment".
"This announcement is slightly disappointing for France Telecom," a London-based industry analyst said, asking not to be indentified.
"But it will not impact the market flotation," he added. The French state is set to sell a minority strake in France Telecom through an Initial Public Offering (IPO) starting May 27.

Concert, which is a pact between British Telecom Plc and MCI Communications, Global One and an alliance of AT&T and Unisource are all trying to create a network of telecoms services around the globe to catch lucrative international business clients.
"The deal with Telefonica gives Concert good access to Latin America. You could say that it gives an advance to Concert over Global One," said another analyst.
"It may make BT and MCI more attractive to an Asian partner," he added.
Both Global One and Concert have made no secret of their intention to line up an Asian ally for their network and Japan's NTT is actively courted.
In Latin America, France Telecom has a small stake in Mexico's Telmex and a 20 percent stake in Telecom Argentina which operates in the north of Argentina.
"France Telecom has some activities in Latin America and so does Sprint, but it does not compare with what Telefonica brings to Concert," an analyst said.
Another analyst noted that the announcement by Telefonica was the second bit of bad news for Global One in as many days.

On Thursday a court in Germany ruled against Global One and in favour of British Telecom who had complained the Deutsche Telekom alliance had started its activities before it had obtained approval by the European Union authorities.
"This shows that there will be no protection for the incumbent operator by the government. It means we will see rapid price erosion," an analyst said.
Global One was set up in 1996 as an extension of the Franco-German Atlas venture. France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom also hold a 10 percent stake in Sprint.

ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said in a recent study on France Telecom about Global One that it was better placed in the international markets than any of the other alliances because "it has a presence at one or more ends of 16 out of the 24 most important routes of the world".
Financial analysts declined to be quoted by name because of sensitivities related to the pending France Telecom privatisation.
